schemes.name: Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS)
schemes.benefit: The government pays all interest during the course and one year after (the moratorium), on loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh
schemes.how_to_apply: Ask the lending bank for CSIS when taking the education loan; there is no separate application

provenance.source_name: Ministry of Education scheme rules (via bank and news summaries)
provenance.evidence: CSIS: 100 % interest subsidy during the moratorium (course + 1 year) for family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh, on loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh; full-time technical/professional courses; applied through the lending bank (Tata Capital and other lender summaries). Confirm current rules with the bank.

schemes.name: PM-Vidyalaxmi
schemes.why: Only for students admitted to top-ranked institutions (QHEIs); check your college.
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free, guarantor-free education loans; 75 % government credit guarantee on loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh; 3 % interest subvention during the moratorium on loans up to Rs 10 lakh for family income up to Rs 8 lakh
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal; banks process applications there

provenance.source_name: PM-Vidyalaxmi scheme (Cabinet approval Nov 2024; portal launched Feb 2025)
provenance.evidence: Collateral- and guarantor-free loans for QHEI students; 75 % credit guarantee up to Rs 7.5 lakh; 3 % interest subvention on loans up to Rs 10 lakh for family income up to Rs 8 lakh; not combinable with other government scholarships or interest subvention (Business Standard, Business Today, Careers360 reports).

plain_language: You borrow Rs 800,000. Usually nothing is paid while studying and for one year after (60 months).
Interest still adds up in that time: about Rs 25,000, so you owe about Rs 825,000 when repayment starts.
Over 10 years that is about Rs 10,902 a month, Rs 1,308,240 in total.
A longer loan means a smaller EMI but more interest in total.
The 10-year EMI is about 33% of today's monthly family income.
cautions: The 10.0% rate is an estimate. Banks quote different rates; compare at least two.
Ask whether interest during the course is simple or compound, and whether you can pay it as you go.
Loans above Rs 7.5 lakh may need collateral or a guarantor, except under PM-Vidyalaxmi.
Scheme rules change. Confirm with the bank or the official portal before applying.
